NEWS UPDATE: The four UP students and two youth activists arrested along Kalaw Avenue, Manila during the Labor Day protest May 1, 2024, have now been cleared of all criminal charges.

The final charge of direct assault filed against the individuals was dismissed by the Metropolitan Trial Court of Manila Thursday based on reasonable doubt, fully clearing the Mayo Uno 6.

The malicious mischief charge had been dismissed for lack of probable cause June 20, 2024 and the illegal assembly charge was dismissed for insufficiency of prosecution evidence March 13.

The group’s legal counsel also asserted that the arresting officers be held accountable for their use of excessive force. They likewise criticized the police’s use of Batas Pambansa 880, a Marcos-era law predating the current constitution, to justify their arbitrary arrests of protesters.

“This acquittal is not just a legal victory—it’s a reminder that the streets belong to the people,” said Mark Vincent Lim, one of the six’s lawyers.

RELATED: https://t.co/Akr6MOdQws
